headline: Nasdaq-100 futures extend their recovery off the session low after an orderly cash close, holding Tail in the low band while rotation out of semiconductors keeps Stress elevated
body: The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,725.81, down 434.27 points or 1.39%, inside a 30,556.40 to 31,125.13 session range against a 31,160.08 previous close and a 30,985.23 open, its second consecutive decline from this week's record. December Nasdaq-100 futures, the preferred continuous reference, print 31,021.25 as of 20:59:59Z, down 381.00 points or 1.21% from a 31,402.25 prior settlement, inside a 30,792.50 to 31,466.00 range. The decisive observation for this hour is that the futures low set during the afternoon has now held through the power hour, the 20:00Z cash close and the first post-settlement hour, with price 228.75 points above it and 25.75 points above the level recorded at the previous assessment. That is an observed retracement, not the shallow-pullback structure that defines a pathological path. The driver remains a Financial Times report that OpenAI's annualized revenue stood near $50 billion at the end of September, roughly $20 billion below the figure previously circulated to investors, which sent the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down 3.4% with Intel off about 6% and Arm, Marvell and Micron each down more than 5%. The amplifier stack is not aligned behind that move. The 10-year yield eased to 5.23% from a 5.33% session high, the 30-year sits near 5.61% after a 5.618% auction stop, WTI crude at 91.18 is 2.02 below its 93.20 high after the Iran timeline comment pared the advance, and the VIX at 15.41 remains low in absolute terms despite a 2.19% rise. Breadth corroborates rotation rather than index-wide liquidation: the Dow closed up 0.10% and the Russell 2000 up 0.03% against the Nasdaq-100's 1.39% decline, and initial jobless claims fell to 197,000. Bitcoin near $81,000 at a three-week low is the one cross-asset reading still pointing the other way. The unresolved question is the Asian handover, where Tokyo and Seoul price the chip repricing for the first time from 00:00Z; the single Asia-Pacific indication available at this cutoff has ASX futures 19 points higher at 8,715, which does not support a gap-down panic read. Shared Finviz context was unusable this run, reporting partial collection with a timestamp roughly nine days old, so it was excluded and the assessment rests on independently verified primary sources.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours opened with a quiet mean-reverting overnight tape: Tail decayed from 12 at 21:00Z on October 7 to a cycle low of 10 at 03:00Z while Stress held a 47 to 53 range. From 06:00Z the crude and long-end-yield impulse took over, Tail stepping to 22 at 07:00Z and then holding a 20 to 23 watch-band range through the European and early United States session as Stress climbed from 55 to a 59 to 66 plateau. The 14:00Z slot eased to 17 on an orderly cash open before 15:00Z and 16:00Z returned to 20 and 22. The single block-band hour in the window is 17:00Z at Tail 28 and Stress 72, published as the semiconductor decline reached its widest extension; 18:00Z and 19:00Z returned to 21 and 22 as the session low held, and 20:00Z closed the window at 18 once the cash close printed 169 points above it. Every one of the 24 slots is available from published Claude history and none has been revised with hindsight.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in the low band at 17 for the current post-close hour and 22:00Z, because the 30,792.50 futures low has now survived the power hour, the cash close and the first post-settlement hour while every amplifier finished below its session high. The named overnight checkpoint is the Asian handover: 23:00Z is lifted to 19 for the Tokyo and Sydney pre-open and 00:00Z and 01:00Z enter the watch band at 20 because Tokyo and Seoul price the OpenAI revenue revision and the 3.4% semiconductor decline for the first time, with a chip-led gap that extends without retracement as the stated escalation mechanism and ASX futures 19 points higher at 8,715 as the counterweight. Tail steps back to 19 at 02:00Z as the danger window closes and decays to a 17 to 18 baseline through the Asian afternoon, then lifts to 18 and 19 across the European pre-open and cash open as ASML and the European chip proxies price the theme. The second watch-band cluster is the Friday United States session: 13:00Z sits at 19 for the cash open, 14:00Z is the densest checkpoint in the forecast at 21 because preliminary October University of Michigan sentiment and inflation expectations print inside the first half hour after the open, and 15:00Z holds 20 while that release is digested. Tail returns to a 18 to 19 range through the afternoon, lifting at 19:00Z for the power hour and weekly expiry unwind and closing the window at 19 for the 20:00Z cash close and the scheduled Fed Collins speech. Stress stays in a 62 to 69 band throughout, high relative to Tail, which is the intended separation when rotation and event risk coexist with orderly price discovery.
